findings.title: Denial-cache test does not actually prove the denial cache short-circuits
findings.body: The test "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" claims to "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but it seeds the permission cache with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, i.e. the scope maps to false, so `checkPermission` would deny anyway (and with no store configured the fallback path would also deny). The test therefore passes even if the permission-denial cache lookup were removed entirely, so the new behaviour is untested. Set the scope to `true` so that a deny result can only come from the denial cache.

findings.title: Every negative Check for a new resource name triggers a full permission DB query
findings.body: Check now falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB query for basic roles, teams and permissions) whenever the cached scope map does not grant access, and only caches the negative result per (namespace, user, action, name, parent). Since `name` is caller-supplied, a client repeatedly checking distinct resource names the user cannot access produces one full permissions query per distinct name within each 30s window, bypassing the permission cache entirely. This is a significant and attacker-influenceable increase in DB load compared to the previous behaviour where the cached scope map answered denials. Consider caching a "permissions freshly loaded" marker per user/action so at most one DB refresh happens per TTL.

findings.title: Denial cache key can collide between distinct (name, parent) pairs
findings.body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` joins namespace, user, action, name and parent with a single `_` separator and name/parent are arbitrary UIDs that may contain `_`. For example name="a", parent="b_c" and name="a_b", parent="c" produce the same key, so a denial recorded for one resource can deny a different resource for up to the cache TTL. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs or length-prefix the components.

findings.title: permissionCacheUsage metric records a miss on cache hits that denied
findings.body: When `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeds but `checkPermission` returns false, execution falls through to line 137, which increments `permissionCacheUsage` with label "false" (miss) even though the permission cache was actually hit. The cache hit-rate metric will therefore understate hits for all deny paths, making it unreliable for tuning the cache.

findings.title: Denial cache delays visibility of newly granted permissions with no invalidation path
findings.body: A negative result is cached for `shortCacheTTL` (30s) keyed per resource, and nothing invalidates it when a permission is granted (e.g. a user is added to a role/team or given access to an existing dashboard). Previously such a grant became visible when the per-user permission cache expired; now the deny answer is sticky for up to 30s after the grant with no way to clear it. Worth documenting, or wiring an invalidation on permission writes.
